changes: Restrict reference/current tract pole matching to the original usable band; retain the reconstruction colour envelope above it without inverting a folded low-frequency image.
Periodic-only 300-Hz bell, Q 0.8: 0.6 dB at 16 kHz, 0.7 dB at 22.05 kHz, 0.8 dB at 32 kHz, 0.92 dB at 44.1 kHz and 1 dB at 48 kHz. AH and AF do not enter this bell.
Remove the overwritten legacy fit in Classic mode; reuse atomically published immutable clock curves; skip a new voice fit in silent voiced-tract frames.
ECI interface and German Z context rule unchanged.

checks.nvda_driver_en: 24 initial-language cases; selectable, x64, FIFO, indices/done, cancel/close passed
checks.nvda_driver_de: 24 initial-language cases; selectable, x64, FIFO, indices/done, cancel/close passed

voice_dsp_replay.dataset: Native EN-US and German example sentences from test_eci_classic_voice_stability.py; male model at 16/22.05/32/48 kHz. Captured from dev6 and replayed through each core.
voice_dsp_replay.measurement: Three isolated replay processes per version; process user CPU time measured by resource.getrusage, median; same host and compiler options. No Windows/ARM measurement.
voice_dsp_replay.peak_measurement: Raw float core samples before host gain and PCM conversion; do not interpret the raw value as a public PCM16 peak.

limits: Windows x64 DLL cross-built and PE-verified. Windows runtime checks run separately in GitHub Actions.
The 44.5% reduction concerns this native DSP replay, not total NVDA latency or Windows-on-ARM execution.
Actual listening and underruns on the user device still require the NVDA test. No claim of subjective identity or all-input clipping freedom.
Existing provider LTO maybe-uninitialized warnings remain visible.
